binders: A real m by m matrix A indexed by Fin m.
conclusions: A has real eigenvalues and an indexed real eigenbasis if and only if there exist real eigenvalues lambda_p and an indexed family v_p of m real m-vectors which is linearly independent and satisfies A v_p=lambda_p v_p for every p.
mathematical_definitions: The left-side hyperbolicity predicate requires an actual Module.Basis indexed by Fin m, all of whose members are eigenvectors.
The right-side eigenvectors form a function Fin m -> (Fin m -> Real).
Linear independence means injectivity of the finitely supported linear-combination map.
translation.proposition_plain_english: A real m by m matrix possesses a complete real eigenbasis exactly when it has m indexed linearly independent real eigenvectors, each with a corresponding real eigenvalue.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No symmetry or other structural assumption on A is made.
Eigenvalues need not be distinct, ordered, or unique, and eigenvectors are not normalized.
The right side does not explicitly state spanning; because it gives exactly m linearly independent vectors in Real^m, the asserted equivalence promotes them to a basis.
Linear independence forces each vector in a nonempty indexed family to be nonzero, so a separate nonzero clause is absent.
The dimension m may be zero; both the empty basis formulation and empty linearly independent family are valid.
The statement is purely algebraic and encodes no PDE or propagation semantics.
